title: Exit Polls Show Tight Israeli Election as High Turnout Leaves Blocs Short of Majority
summary: Preliminary exit polls from Israel's parliamentary election suggest no clear path to a 61-seat governing majority for either Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu or his centrist challenger Gadi Eisenkot, despite historic voter participation.
body: Israel held its parliamentary general election on Tuesday, marked by surging voter participation and preliminary exit poll projections that left neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his leading challenger with a clear route to a governing majority in the 120-seat Knesset.

The contest featured Netanyahu, leader of the right-wing Likud party, facing a prominent general election challenge from former military chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, who heads the centrist Yashar party. Forming a government in Israel requires assembling a coalition of at least 61 seats, a threshold that neither major political camp appeared poised to reach easily based on early polling projections.

While exit polls and Likud officials indicated that Likud remained the largest single party in the Knesset, projections diverged regarding the balance of power between the broader blocs. The Guardian reported that exit polls pointed to the opposition bloc led by Eisenkot winning slightly more seats than Netanyahu's right-wing alliance. In contrast, exit poll data cited by Al Jazeera placed the Eisenkot-led bloc and Netanyahu's coalition in a dead heat at 51 seats each.

According to exit poll figures reported by Al Jazeera, Arab parties were projected to win 18 seats. However, a coalition agreement involving them appears unlikely, as both Netanyahu and Eisenkot previously ruled out entering into a formal governing partnership with Arab factions, with Eisenkot citing a lack of shared values.

Voter engagement remained unusually high throughout the day. The Central Elections Committee noted that turnout reached 44.9 percent by 2:00 PM, marking the highest midday voting rate recorded in an Israeli election since 1973. Al Jazeera reported that the committee placed final voter turnout at approximately 77.7 percent, with more than 5.69 million of the country's roughly 7.33 million eligible voters casting ballots after officials denied a request from Likud to extend voting beyond the scheduled 10:00 PM closure.

With official vote tallies and certified seat distributions still to be finalized, the preliminary numbers suggest that Israel could face prolonged coalition negotiations. If neither major faction succeeds in assembling the requisite 61-seat majority, Netanyahu could remain in office in a caretaker capacity while parties navigate the political impasse.

title: Cyclone Arnab Hits India's Eastern Coast, Prompting Evacuations and Alerts Reaching Nepal
summary: Cyclone Arnab has triggered large-scale evacuations in eastern India and weather warnings extending into Nepal, where Himalayan trekking permits have been suspended due to avalanche hazards.
body: Severe weather has disrupted eastern India as Cyclone Arnab approached and began moving ashore. The Hindu reported that the very severe cyclonic storm started its landfall process near Narsapur, bringing heavy rains to Visakhapatnam. Experts from the India Meteorological Department noted that the landfall process could continue for an extended duration, stating that the tentative point of landfall can only be officially determined once the process is complete.

The timeline and progress of the cyclone saw differing accounts in initial international reporting. The New York Times reported that the storm was projected to make landfall on Wednesday along the eastern coast, noting that Indian authorities had already evacuated tens of thousands of residents from threatened areas in anticipation of the storm's arrival.

Meteorological projections show Cyclone Arnab cutting inland and continuing on a northern trajectory toward Nepal. A bulletin issued by Nepal's weather department warned that the cyclone was gaining strength over the Bay of Bengal and was expected to deliver heavy rainfall across the border region.

In response to the deteriorating weather forecasts and the potential for heightened avalanche risks, NDTV reported that authorities in Nepal halted Himalayan trekking permits as the system moved inland.

title: Network Glitch at Mumbai Airport Forces Manual Check-Ins Amid Reports of Flight Delays
summary: A network outage at Mumbai Airport prompted staff to switch to manual check-in and boarding procedures, leading to conflicting accounts between the airport operator and flight tracking data regarding the extent of flight disruptions.
body: A network outage struck Mumbai Airport on Tuesday evening, forcing ground staff to transition to manual processing for passenger check-in and boarding. According to reporting by the Times of India, the technical disruption lasted for approximately one hour.

Mumbai International Airport Ltd, the airport's operator, maintained that flight operations remained unaffected throughout the incident, stating that staff implemented manual procedures to minimize passenger inconvenience. Airport officials did not disclose the root cause of the technical failure.

Despite the operator's statement, flight monitoring services and airline accounts pointed to widespread disruptions across the airport's schedule. Data from Flightradar24, reported by Livemint, indicated that 327 flights experienced delays by roughly 9:30 p.m., with departure delays averaging around 50 minutes.

Airlines further noted that flights had already been experiencing delays due to air traffic control congestion prior to the system crash. According to the Hindustan Times, carriers stated that the subsequent network failure compounded those pre-existing operational delays.

title: Cyclone Arnab Begins Landfall Along India's Eastern Coast as Mass Evacuations Underway
summary: Cyclone Arnab initiated its landfall process along India's eastern coast late on October 27, triggering extensive evacuations, shelter openings, and widespread travel cancellations across Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
body: Coastal regions of eastern India braced for severe weather late on October 27, 2026, as Cyclone Arnab began crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast. According to the India Meteorological Department, the cyclone's northern spiral band entered land late Tuesday night, setting off a landfall process expected to continue for about three hours as heavy rainfall battered the region.

Forecasts on the exact timing and intensity of the crossing fluctuated across official updates. An alert reported by NDTV indicated the storm would cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam between 2 a.m. and 4 a.m., while other assessments pointed to landfall occurring closer to dawn on Wednesday. Projected wind speeds also varied, with reports from The Hindu citing forecasts of 125 to 135 km/h, while Livemint noted projected speeds reaching up to 140 km/h.

State authorities mounted large-scale emergency operations to safeguard coastal populations. According to Livemint, at least 89,000 people were evacuated into more than 2,000 relief shelters across Andhra Pradesh, while neighboring Odisha outlined plans to evacuate 48,000 residents. Wider reports confirmed that thousands had been moved out of danger zones, and Andhra Pradesh officials secured approximately 30,000 fishing boats ashore.

The severe weather brought widespread transit disruptions across both states. Train services were halted, several flights were cancelled, and Odisha shut ghat roads alongside broader transport curbs. Amid the operational impact, the Civil Aviation Ministry reviewed flight safety conditions, and airlines were advised to follow adverse weather protocols, keep travelers updated on delays and cancellations, and adhere to passenger refund and rebooking requirements.

title: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro Reportedly Departs for US Amid Criminal Investigations
summary: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has reportedly left Brazil for the United States following his loss in Sunday's presidential election to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, even as federal police report no official border exit record and an outstanding Supreme Court passport surrender order remains unfulfilled.
body: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has reportedly left Brazil and is traveling to the United States following his defeat in Sunday's presidential election against left-wing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, according to media reports citing sources close to the lawmaker.

Bolsonaro's reported departure comes in the midst of ongoing legal probes in Brazil, where authorities are investigating him for corruption, money laundering, and tax evasion. The Supreme Court had previously issued an order requiring the senator to surrender his passport, but he missed the official deadline to hand the document over.

The circumstances and route of Bolsonaro's travel remain unclear. Brazilian Federal Police confirmed that there is no official entry or exit record showing him departing through any recognized migration checkpoint. Furthermore, political allies reported attempting to contact Bolsonaro on Tuesday morning without receiving any response.

Meanwhile, the U.S. State Department announced that it will issue visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family. The senator held tacit backing from Donald Trump, whose administration had previously claimed that Bolsonaro's father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, was the victim of judicial persecution in Brazil.

title: Flávio Bolsonaro Departs for U.S. Following Brazil Election Loss
summary: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has left Brazil for the United States after losing the presidential runoff to incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, defying a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports.
body: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has left the country for the United States following his presidential election defeat to incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. A senior U.S. State Department official confirmed on Tuesday that the United States will grant entry visas to Bolsonaro and his family.

The move follows an order by Brazil's Supreme Court demanding Bolsonaro surrender his passports within 24 hours as part of an ongoing money laundering investigation. The court raised concerns that Bolsonaro had the financial means to leave Brazil, though Bolsonaro has denied any wrongdoing. According to reporting by Reuters cited by the Times of India, a senior Brazilian Federal Police official stated that Bolsonaro did not leave through any standard border or migration checkpoints, and his passports were canceled after the deadline passed.

The departure marks a sharp turn from Bolsonaro's stated plans on Monday, when he said he would remain in Brazil, hand over his documents, and take on the role of opposition leader. His campaign manager expressed surprise at news of his exit. President Lula criticized the departure as shameful, remarking that Bolsonaro should have remained in the country to defend himself against the accusations.

The election results have also drawn contrasting reactions. Bolsonaro initially indicated he would seek to annul the runoff over alleged irregularities, but his own Liberal Party officially conceded defeat to Lula on Monday, with Al Jazeera reporting the margin of victory at over 4.4 million votes. Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump claimed without evidence that the contest appeared rigged, though reports indicated that no evidence of electoral fraud has emerged.
